title: The Scientific & Intellectual Revolutions
subject: Science, Technology, and Society
description: Four dimensions of science, the Engine of Discovery, Cradles of Early Science (Mesoamerica, Asia, Middle East, Africa), and the Copernican, Darwinian, and Freudian paradigm shifts.
sourceFile: The Scientific Revolution (1).pdf, STS-WK1-MTWThF A book reference in STS.pdf, STS MIDTERM REVIEWER.docx

questions.question: Which dimension defines science as 'a subject, discipline, field of study, or body of knowledge dealing with learning about the natural and physical world'?
options: Science as an Idea
Science as an Intellectual Activity
Science as a Body of Knowledge
Science as a Personal and Social Activity
questions.answer: Science as a Body of Knowledge
questions.explanation: The four dimensions are Idea (theories/explanations), Intellectual Activity (observation/experimentation), Body of Knowledge (academic discipline), and Personal/Social Activity.

questions.question: When and where did the European Scientific Revolution occur, and what personal traits drove its scientists according to the slides and midterm reviewer?
options: 16th to 18th century in Europe; driven by creativity, curiosity, critical thinking, and deep passion to discover—not clamor for publicity
5th century BCE in Egypt; driven solely by royal military decrees
20th century in Antarctica; driven by social media fame
12th century in Rome; driven by avoidance of observation
questions.answer: 16th to 18th century in Europe; driven by creativity, curiosity, critical thinking, and deep passion to discover—not clamor for publicity
questions.explanation: Creativity, curiosity, and critical thinking drove scientists to generate science ideas, discoveries, and technology, often facing persecution.

questions.question: During the Golden Age of Islam in the Middle East, which scholar is paired with Optics, Algorithms/Algebra, Chemistry, and Clinical Pharmacology respectively?
options: Ibn al-Haytham (Optics), al-Khwarizmi (Algorithms/Algebra), Jabir ibn Hayyan (Chemistry), Ibn Sina (Clinical pharmacology)
Ptolemy (Optics), Copernicus (Algebra), Darwin (Chemistry), Freud (Pharmacology)
Aryabhata (Optics), Galileo (Algebra), Pasteur (Chemistry), Kier (Pharmacology)
Plato (Optics), Aristotle (Algebra), Newton (Chemistry), Gutenberg (Pharmacology)
questions.answer: Ibn al-Haytham (Optics), al-Khwarizmi (Algorithms/Algebra), Jabir ibn Hayyan (Chemistry), Ibn Sina (Clinical pharmacology)
questions.explanation: The Middle East placed strong value on empirical science experiments through pioneers like Ibn al-Haytham, al-Khwarizmi, Jabir ibn Hayyan, and Ibn Sina.

questions.question: Which early Asian achievements are highlighted in 'Cradles of Early Science'?
options: India: Ayurveda, early spherical Earth theories, Aryabhata's trigonometry, Mohenjo-daro ruler; China: acupuncture, compass, papermaking, gunpowder, printing, first seismological detector
India: Gutenberg press and clepsydra; China: Roman numerals and pyramids
India: Darwinian evolution; China: psychoanalytic dream analysis
India: chinampas; China: quipu knotted cords
questions.answer: India: Ayurveda, early spherical Earth theories, Aryabhata's trigonometry, Mohenjo-daro ruler; China: acupuncture, compass, papermaking, gunpowder, printing, first seismological detector
questions.explanation: Both India and China made foundational scientific and technological contributions long before modern European science.

questions.question: Whose cosmological model dominated Western thought for roughly 1,500 years prior to Copernicus, placing an immobile Earth at the center of the universe?
options: Johannes Kepler
Claudius Ptolemy (Geocentric Model)
Isaac Newton
Galileo Galilei
questions.answer: Claudius Ptolemy (Geocentric Model)
questions.explanation: Ptolemy's geocentric model held that the sun, moon, and planets revolved around a stationary Earth and was endorsed by Church doctrine.

questions.question: What was Nicolaus Copernicus's primary method in formulating heliocentrism, and what 1543 publication officially sparked the Scientific Revolution?
options: Deep-space radio telescopes; 'On the Origin of Species'
A profound 'thought experiment' (rather than extensive physical testing); 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium' (1543)
Sea voyages to the Galapagos; 'Commentariolus'
Free association interviews; 'The Descent of Man'
questions.answer: A profound 'thought experiment' (rather than extensive physical testing); 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium' (1543)
questions.explanation: Copernicus drafted his ideas in Commentariolus (1508–1514) and published De revolutionibus orbium coelestium in 1543.

questions.question: In Copernicus's early manuscript 'Commentariolus,' what triple motion of the Earth did he propose?
options: Melting, freezing, and boiling
Daily rotation on its axis, annual revolution around the Sun, and axial precession
Tectonic drift, ocean tides, and volcanic eruption
Linear gravity, elliptical warping, and solar eclipse
questions.answer: Daily rotation on its axis, annual revolution around the Sun, and axial precession
questions.explanation: Copernicus posited Earth's daily axial rotation, yearly solar orbit, and gradual axial precession.

questions.question: How did Copernicus's heliocentric model explain the apparent backward (retrograde) motion of outer planets?
options: Planets randomly reverse direction whenever comets pass
It is an optical illusion caused by Earth overtaking slower outer planets in its faster orbit around the Sun
The Sun orbits the Moon every thirty days
The Catholic Church decreed the stars were static
questions.answer: It is an optical illusion caused by Earth overtaking slower outer planets in its faster orbit around the Sun
questions.explanation: Heliocentrism eliminated Ptolemy's cumbersome equants by explaining retrograde motion naturally via relative orbital speeds.

questions.question: Which geometric flaw did Copernicus retain in his heliocentric model that was later corrected by Johannes Kepler?
options: He placed the Moon at the center of the galaxy
He retained circular orbits and epicycles instead of elliptical orbits
He claimed Earth had no gravity
He omitted Mercury and Venus
questions.answer: He retained circular orbits and epicycles instead of elliptical orbits
questions.explanation: Kepler later demonstrated that planetary orbits are ellipses rather than perfect circles.

questions.question: Why did the Catholic Church initially reject and ban Copernicus's heliocentric model in the 16th century?
options: Because his math was written in Chinese characters
It was judged heretical for contradicting prevailing religious beliefs that Earth was created first at the center of the universe
Because Copernicus refused to use Latin
Because astronomers proved the Sun orbited Jupiter
questions.answer: It was judged heretical for contradicting prevailing religious beliefs that Earth was created first at the center of the universe
questions.explanation: Despite persecution and Church bans, astronomers gradually adopted heliocentrism because it resolved geocentric inconsistencies and launched modern astronomy.

questions.question: Before Charles Darwin's evolutionary theory, what was the dominant view regarding species and human origins?
options: Species evolved continuously via random mutations
Biblical design: humans held a privileged special creation and species were static and unchanging over time
All organisms evolved from ocean algae within ten years
Humanity was shaped solely by unconscious dreams
questions.answer: Biblical design: humans held a privileged special creation and species were static and unchanging over time
questions.explanation: Darwinism challenged static creationism and anthropocentrism with an evidence-based evolutionary framework.

questions.question: What five-year expedition heavily shaped Charles Darwin's observational evidence for natural selection?
options: A desert trek across Mesopotamia
A survey voyage aboard the HMS Beagle, especially observations at the Galápagos Islands
A polar expedition to Antarctica using satellites
A submarine dive to the Mariana Trench
questions.answer: A survey voyage aboard the HMS Beagle, especially observations at the Galápagos Islands
questions.explanation: Darwin's specimen collection and extraordinary observational skills aboard HMS Beagle underpinned his theory.

questions.question: In his 1859 landmark book 'On the Origin of Species,' what mechanism did Darwin propose to explain how populations adapt and evolve over generations?
options: Natural selection ('descent with modification')
Heliocentric gravitation
Psychoanalytic repression
Spontaneous alchemy
questions.answer: Natural selection ('descent with modification')
questions.explanation: Traits enhancing survival and reproduction in a given environment are passed on, gradually transforming populations.

questions.question: How did Darwin's 1871 book 'The Descent of Man' extend his evolutionary framework?
options: It argued humans were immune to evolution
It applied evolution directly to human origins and introduced Sexual Selection (mate competition and choice) to explain traits like sexual dimorphism
It proposed that planets evolve through natural selection
It introduced the id, ego, and superego
questions.answer: It applied evolution directly to human origins and introduced Sexual Selection (mate competition and choice) to explain traits like sexual dimorphism
questions.explanation: The Descent of Man placed humans within the animal kingdom, overturning anthropocentrism.

questions.question: Philosophically, what two long-held doctrines did the Darwinian Revolution replace with empirical, naturalistic science?
options: Empiricism and heliocentrism
Teleology (fixed divine design governing nature) and anthropocentrism (humans as separate from the animal kingdom)
Mathematics and astronomy
Structuralism and functionalism
questions.answer: Teleology (fixed divine design governing nature) and anthropocentrism (humans as separate from the animal kingdom)
questions.explanation: Evolution shifted biology from supernatural teleology and human exceptionalism to evidence-based observation.

questions.question: Before Freud, who established the first psychology laboratory in 1879 (Structuralism via introspection) and who championed Functionalism?
options: Wilhelm Wundt (Structuralism); William James (Functionalism)
Nicolaus Copernicus; Charles Darwin
Isaac Newton; Galileo Galilei
John Dewey; Immanuel Kant
questions.answer: Wilhelm Wundt (Structuralism); William James (Functionalism)
questions.explanation: Psychology transitioned from philosophy toward science through Wundt's 1879 lab, James's Functionalism, and Freud's clinical psychoanalysis.

questions.question: Prior to Sigmund Freud, how was psychology commonly classified, and what assumption did society hold about human rationality?
options: Classified as nuclear physics; humans viewed as robots
Classified under philosophy/art rather than science; humans viewed as inherently rational while mental illness was largely misunderstood
Classified as astronomy; humans viewed as purely aquatic
Classified as agronomy; mental disorders did not exist
questions.answer: Classified under philosophy/art rather than science; humans viewed as inherently rational while mental illness was largely misunderstood
questions.explanation: Freud disrupted the assumption of pure human rationality by demonstrating the powerful influence of the unconscious mind.

questions.question: In Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic model of personality, what are the roles of the Id, Ego, and Superego?
options: Id: moral conscience; Ego: animal instincts; Superego: logical compromise
Id: instinctual pleasure-driven drives; Ego: realistic mediating agent; Superego: moral conscience
Id: conscious math skills; Ego: sleeping dreams; Superego: muscle reflexes
Id: social media habits; Ego: short-term memory; Superego: genetics
questions.answer: Id: instinctual pleasure-driven drives; Ego: realistic mediating agent; Superego: moral conscience
questions.explanation: Freud argued that human personality emerges from the ongoing tension among the instinctual id, realistic ego, and moral superego.

questions.question: Which three clinical techniques did Freud use to uncover hidden thoughts and desires inside the unconscious mind?
options: Telescopes, microscopes, and water clocks
Free association, dream analysis, and analyzing slips of the tongue ('Freudian slips')
Natural selection, gene splicing, and carbon dating
Enframing, poiesis, and calculative thinking
questions.answer: Free association, dream analysis, and analyzing slips of the tongue ('Freudian slips')
questions.explanation: Freud used free association, dream interpretation, and verbal slips to probe unconscious conflicts rooted in early childhood.

questions.question: Why did 'science hardliners' initially dismiss Freud's psychoanalysis, and what ultimately earned psychology recognition as a science?
options: Because it lacked experimental/empirical data and felt unorthodox (focusing on sexuality); Freud refined it into an effective clinical method for treating mental disorders
Because Freud refused to publish in German or English
Because psychoanalysis relied exclusively on chemical blood tests
Because Freud claimed the Earth was flat
questions.answer: Because it lacked experimental/empirical data and felt unorthodox (focusing on sexuality); Freud refined it into an effective clinical method for treating mental disorders
questions.explanation: Despite intense academic controversy, Freud's clinical framework helped establish psychology as a recognized scientific discipline.

questions.question: According to the 'Synthesis: The Anatomy of a Paradigm Shift' chart, what was the source of controversy for Copernicus, Darwin, and Freud respectively?
options: Copernicus: heresy against the Catholic Church; Darwin: challenged religious/unscientific ideas of human origin; Freud: unorthodox focus on human sexuality and inner nature
All three were criticized solely for poor spelling
Copernicus: high printing costs; Darwin: ocean piracy; Freud: lack of hospital beds
Copernicus: alchemy; Darwin: meteorology; Freud: astrophysics
questions.answer: Copernicus: heresy against the Catholic Church; Darwin: challenged religious/unscientific ideas of human origin; Freud: unorthodox focus on human sexuality and inner nature
questions.explanation: Each thinker overturned deeply entrenched cultural dogma and provoked initial resistance before transforming science.

questions.question: What common lesson do the Copernican, Darwinian, and Freudian revolutions reveal about how science relates to society?
options: Scientific revolutions operate completely isolated from public beliefs
Scientific breakthroughs challenge dominant dogma, reshape human self-understanding, and transform society's worldview
Society immediately accepts every revolutionary scientific idea without debate
Only ancient Greek theories can ever be valid
questions.answer: Scientific breakthroughs challenge dominant dogma, reshape human self-understanding, and transform society's worldview
questions.explanation: Intellectual revolutions demonstrate the deep two-way interaction between scientific inquiry and societal beliefs.

questions.question: What famous motto did Nicolaus Copernicus declare regarding the technical rigor of his astronomical work?
options: 'Earth is the immovable throne of creation.'
'Mathematics is written for mathematicians.'
'The unconscious never sleeps.'
'Only the fittest survive.'
questions.answer: 'Mathematics is written for mathematicians.'
questions.explanation: Copernicus underscored the mathematical foundation of his heliocentric astronomy with this statement.

questions.question: Eventually, how did many people reconcile Charles Darwin's theory of evolution with religious faith?
options: By banning biology from all schools
By recognizing that evolution was not inherently against Church teachings and that science and faith can coexist
By replacing natural selection with geocentrism
By declaring all species ceased changing in 1859
questions.answer: By recognizing that evolution was not inherently against Church teachings and that science and faith can coexist
questions.explanation: The textbook notes that after intense debate, people came to see that evolution and religious faith need not be mutually exclusive.

questions.question: How did the Midterm Reviewer trace the three major phases of the Information Revolution?
options: 1. Language & Mathematics (meta phusis & Newton) -> 2. Gutenberg's 15th-century printing press -> 3. Tim Berners-Lee's World Wide Web at CERN
1. Gunpowder -> 2. Kerosene -> 3. Amphibious tricycles
1. Hieroglyphics -> 2. Coal mining -> 3. Gene therapy
1. Telegraph -> 2. Papyrus -> 3. Water clock
questions.answer: 1. Language & Mathematics (meta phusis & Newton) -> 2. Gutenberg's 15th-century printing press -> 3. Tim Berners-Lee's World Wide Web at CERN
questions.explanation: Information evolved from spoken/written language and mathematical laws to printed mass media and global digital networks.

questions.question: In ancient Egypt (Africa), beyond pyramids, which scientific fields were notably practiced according to the Scientific Revolution slides?
options: Geometry for Nile land boundaries, advanced alchemy, human anatomy, and solar/lunar calendars
Quantum computing and stem cell therapy
Locomotive railways and telegraph cables
Oil refining and nuclear fission
questions.answer: Geometry for Nile land boundaries, advanced alchemy, human anatomy, and solar/lunar calendars
questions.explanation: Egyptians applied practical geometry along the Nile alongside astronomy, anatomy, and early chemistry/alchemy.

questions.question: In the 'Scientific Revolution' slides, why did the Golden Age of Islam accelerate scientific progress?
options: Scholars placed greater value on empirical science experiments rather than relying solely on abstract thought
Islamic scholars forbade translating Greek or Indian manuscripts
They banned all mathematical treatises
They relied exclusively on oral poetry
questions.answer: Scholars placed greater value on empirical science experiments rather than relying solely on abstract thought
questions.explanation: Empirical experimentation in optics, chemistry, medicine, and mathematics flourished during the Islamic Golden Age.

questions.question: According to 'The Engine of Discovery' diagram in the Scientific Revolution slides, what three outputs emerge from scientists combining Creativity, Curiosity, and Critical Thinking?
options: Science Ideas, Science Discoveries, and Technology
Fame, Political Office, and Military Conquest
Dogma, Superstition, and Secrecy
Patents, Advertising, and Censorship
questions.answer: Science Ideas, Science Discoveries, and Technology
questions.explanation: Scientists' curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking produce scientific ideas, discoveries, and technological innovations.

questions.question: According to Freud, what powerfully shapes adult personality, neuroses, and unconscious conflicts?
options: Adult tax brackets
Early childhood experiences and unconscious drives
Planetary positions at birth
Daily caloric intake alone
questions.answer: Early childhood experiences and unconscious drives
questions.explanation: Freud's developmental premise holds that early childhood experiences profoundly shape adult personality and neuroses.

questions.question: How do historical scientific revolutions directly connect to contemporary institutions according to the STS Midterm Reviewer?
options: They have zero relevance to modern society
Cuneiform/papyrus evolved into web servers; irrigation/pasteurization formed modern sanitation/public health; ancient tools laid groundwork for automated supply chains
Modern computers are built out of Sumerian mud bricks
Only 21st-century inventions count as real technology
questions.answer: Cuneiform/papyrus evolved into web servers; irrigation/pasteurization formed modern sanitation/public health; ancient tools laid groundwork for automated supply chains
questions.explanation: Modern technology and public institutions represent cumulative developments rooted in historical antecedents.
